clue.text: Flowery spikes girl placed in gaps

indicators.note: the girl's name is put inside the word for gaps, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

explanation.surface: Someone arranges spiky flowers, with a girl tucking them into empty spots.
explanation.definitionFit: A spadix is a fleshy flower spike, as in arum lilies; the plural form is the botanical term for several.

clue.text: This chemical's spilt when there's no mop here

indicators.note: spilt suggests letters scattered, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: A substance is spilled because no mop is to hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A pheromone is a chemical secreted by animals to signal to others of their species.

clue.text: Journalist taking a new direction with CHIC simple charm

indicators.note: the editor turns round, reading the other way

parts.note: ED, editor, is a senior journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter switches tack, bringing a plain, easy charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking a new direction' turns ED into DE.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm someone is to delight them, give them great pleasure.

clue.text: Gosh, endless entertainment is provided SIT by holiday island!

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like gosh

indicators.note: the word for entertainment loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone enthuses that a holiday island offers non-stop fun.
explanation.definitionFit: Corfu is a Greek island in the Ionian Sea popular with holidaymakers.

clue.text: Ask to play music

indicators.note: play suggests letters moving about freely, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: A band is asked to perform some music.
explanation.definitionFit: Ska is a Jamaican music genre, a forerunner of reggae.

clue.text: Padre perhaps has finished with soldiers

parts.note: OR, other ranks, is the usual abbreviation for ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A retired army chaplain has finished his service with the troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A padre is a military chaplain, one example of a minister in charge of a congregation; 'perhaps' marks the example.

clue.text: Disguise bad news about publication folding?

definitions.meaning: to cover up problems, as in hiding cracks
a newspaper bent back on itself, read literally

explanation.surface: A newspaper going under tries to hide the bad news.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to conceal faults or difficulties, as with decorating over cracks.

clue.text: Fish, any number caught by engineer

indicators.note: the number letter is held inside the engineer's word

parts.note: a sapper is a military engineer
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: An army engineer lands a load of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The snapper is a family of food fish, such as the red snapper.

clue.text: Operating with group making attack

explanation.surface: A working party launches an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: An onset is an attack or assault, as well as a beginning.

clue.text: Room a bit too small for musical instrument

indicators.note: the instrument's word falls a little short, losing its final letter

parts.note: the cello is a stringed musical instrument

explanation.surface: A practice room is just slightly too cramped to fit a large instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery.

clue.text: From judge again receive commendation

parts.note: to reap is to receive, gather the reward

explanation.surface: Someone gets a commendation from the judge on appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassess something is to evaluate or form a judgement on it a second time.

clue.text: Athlete's garment that comes down over the thighs?

definitions.meaning: a field-event competitor who leaps for distance from a run-up

definitions.text: garment that comes down over the thighs?
definitions.meaning: a sweater cut extra long, reaching below the hips, read whimsically

explanation.surface: A sportsman wears a sweater that reaches well down his legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A track-and-field leaper competes in that event; a knitted top of extra length is the second sense.

clue.text: Dad goes round boilers, radiators, weal etc emergency repairman?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Dad goes round boilers, radiators, weal etc emergency repairman?', is garbled by stray page text (boilers, radiators) and no source gives the true wording to parse PA + TCHER
annotationWithheld.clue: Dad goes round boilers, radiators, weal etc emergency repairman?

clue.text: Head chef's item

definitions.meaning: the head or crown, especially a bald one
a savoury paste of meat or fish served as a starter

explanation.surface: A head chef presents one of his dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means the top of the head, and also, accented, a smooth meat paste prepared by cooks.

clue.text: Compare guerrilla fighter with holy man?

parts.note: a Contra was a rebel guerrilla in Nicaragua in the 1980s
ST, saint, is a holy man

explanation.surface: Someone sets a jungle rebel beside a saintly figure to weigh them up.
explanation.definitionFit: To contrast two things is to compare them so as to bring out their differences.

clue.text: A daughter taken in by groups of chaps — time for a bit of a change!

indicators.note: the daughter is held between the two groups of men

parts.note: men, twice over, as the phrase is plural
men, twice over, as the phrase is plural

explanation.surface: A daughter is adopted by a set of men and it changes things a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'groups of chaps' gives MEN twice, with D between.
explanation.definitionFit: An amendment is a small alteration, as to a law or text.

clue.text: To a great degree, it is hidden truth

indicators.note: the little word is tucked away inside the intensifier, one piece within another

parts.note: very means to a great degree

explanation.surface: The truth is mostly concealed.
explanation.definitionFit: Verity is a formal word for truth or a true principle.

clue.text: Fighter making mistake is trapped in middle of battle

indicators.note: these pieces are enclosed by the central letters of battle
the central letters of the word are taken

explanation.surface: A soldier errs and is caught in the thick of the fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of battle' gives TT, the two central letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrorist is a fighter using violence against civilians for political ends.

clue.text: One of two archbishops in place of worship

definitions.meaning: Frederick ... and his son William were both Archbishops of Canterbury
a building devoted to worship, such as a Hindu or Jewish house of prayer

explanation.surface: A pair of senior bishops meet in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: Frederick Temple and his son William both became Archbishop of Canterbury, head of the Church of England, in the twentieth century or just before.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of two Canterbury primates is also the common word for a building used for worship.

clue.text: The first woman to criticise another

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly

explanation.surface: The first woman to find fault with another.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Pandora was the first woman, made by the gods.
explanation.definitionFit: Greek mythology names her as the first mortal woman, who opened the jar of evils.

clue.text: Pornography's most dedicated bunch

definitions.meaning: explicit, extreme sexual material; the 's stands for 'is' and joins the two senses
the committed inner core of a group of supporters

explanation.surface: The keenest fans of adult films form a devoted clique.
explanation.definitionFit: The term describes extremely explicit porn and also the loyal nucleus of any movement.

clue.text: Animal on mountain looks down on a tree

indicators.note: in a down clue the animal sits on top of the mountain
the earlier pieces stand above the next one in the column

explanation.surface: A cat perched on a peak gazes down at a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The catalpa is a flowering tree with large heart-shaped leaves and long pods.

clue.text: Embargo imposed on old port

indicators.note: the ban is placed after the letter for old, building on it

explanation.surface: A trade embargo is enforced on an ancient harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: OBAN is a fishing and ferry port on the west coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish west-coast town is a harbour for ferries to the Hebrides, a port by function.

clue.text: It's British to endure severe reprimand

explanation.surface: Putting up with a stern telling-off is a British trait.
explanation.definitionFit: A blast is a severe reprimand or angry criticism.

clue.text: Vain editor's unreliable source

indicators.note: unreliable suggests something not fixed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A conceited newspaper editor relies on a dubious informant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unreliable' tells you to rearrange the letters of VAIN EDITOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A derivation is where a word or thing comes from, its origin or source.

clue.text: Essential ingredient finally placed in The Times medicine container

indicators.note: the letter is put inside the container

parts.note: a vial is a small bottle for medicine

indicators.note: the final letter of ingredient is taken

explanation.surface: A key ingredient goes into a medicine bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: Vital means essential, absolutely necessary.

clue.text: Be very surprised, finding a tile slipping down?

definitions.meaning: an idiom for being astonished, said when promising to eat headgear if proved wrong
tile is slang for a hat, and slipping down suggests it being swallowed

explanation.surface: A roof tile slides off, to someone's amazement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tile' is old British slang for a hat; the second reading pictures a hat going down someone's throat.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is said to express disbelief, promising to consume headgear if something happens.

clue.text: Arrogance half concealed in centre of activity

indicators.note: half of the word is kept out of sight, leaving the first half

explanation.surface: Smugness is partly hidden at the heart of the action.
explanation.definitionFit: A hub is the focal point of activity, like the centre of a wheel.

clue.text: Set out, but face the wrong way

indicators.note: facing the wrong way means read back to front

parts.note: a dial is the face of a clock or watch

explanation.surface: Someone lies down but turns to face backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid out means set out or arranged, as a table or body is.

clue.text: Member of royal family, or of the upper classes in origin

indicators.note: the class letter is put inside the word for origin

parts.note: U is the label for upper-class usage

explanation.surface: A royal is either one of the family or of noble birth.
explanation.walkthrough: U, as in 'U and non-U', is the British label for upper-class speech and manners.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stuarts were the royal house ruling Scotland and later England from the 14th to the 18th century.

clue.text: Noble act excitingly conveyed in style of singing

indicators.note: something done excitingly is stirred up, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A heroic deed is told in thrilling operatic song.
explanation.definitionFit: Bel canto is the Italian lyrical, smooth operatic singing style.
